decision.quote: Our results find general support for Sanders and Carpenter’s (1998) central premise that internationalization shapes firm governance structures but also highlight important non-findings that reflect how the internationalization-governance relationship has changed since their study. Based on the findings of our replication, we also extend Sanders and Carpenter’s (1998) framework and find that firms have more recently coped with the uncertainty of internationalization by hiring CEOs with international experience and hiring a more internationally diverse board of directors. We also provide insights on important boundary conditions of the non-replicated results in our study.
decision.reason: The newly recovered primary publisher abstract explicitly states that the study conducts a replication of Sanders and Carpenter (1998) across their tested internationalization-governance relationships (CEO pay, top management team size, board size and independence, and CEO-chair separation). In their overall summary of the replication results, the authors present the evidence as partly supporting and partly failing to support the original study: they report 'general support for Sanders and Carpenter’s (1998) central premise that internationalization shapes firm governance structures' alongside 'important non-findings that reflect how the internationalization-governance relationship has changed since their study' and explicitly refer to 'the non-replicated results in our study.' Under Step 3 of the codebook, when the authors themselves frame their replication evidence as partly supporting the original work and partly yielding non-replicated findings, the outcome is 'mixed' rather than 'successful'.
